text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 use runs above peers at every complexity level, including many low-complexity patients, but only four documented 99215 claims exist and all were supported, so the records are too thin to call this upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern leans toward concern. The 99215 share exceeds the all-provider rate in every complexity band, and over a third of 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, many with simple diagnoses such as low back pain (C0071409, C0071806), abdominal pain (C0071410) or URI (C0071710). That is the profile more consistent with upcoding than with a sicker panel. The documentation points the other way but cannot carry much weight: all four documented 99215 claims were supported at high MDM, including low-complexity claim C0071775, and the only below-billed finding was a single 99213 (C0071720). The 2 moderate-plus data-reviewed notes without a lab line are weak evidence of templated notes, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims and check whether high MDM is genuinely supported or cloned, then expand the records pull beyond the roughly 3% returned so far."}
